correctness.rationale: The Defant–Kravitz maximum-letter recursion proves both language inclusions, since each lower-alphabet output block can be lifted independently. To check the ambiguous initial concatenation, let B(z) count distinct words in I_{q-1}I_{q-1}. Splitting at successive maximum letters then gives the exact unambiguous block-level series A_q=A_{q-1}+z B/(1-z A_{q-1}), with A_{q-1} coefficientwise <= B <= A_{q-1}^2. The smaller-alphabet growth induction makes A_{q-1} diverge at its radius and z A_{q-1}(z) strictly increase through 1 at an interior first root. On the root circle there are no other zeros of the renewal denominator: the z and z^2 coefficients are positive, so equality in the triangle inequality requires the positive real point. The positive numerator and simple pole give the claimed two-sided exponential bounds (indeed a positive leading constant), and the interior root gives strict monotonicity. In the binary case every word ending in 1 and only those and all-zero words are possible. For larger q the specified four-letter factor would force a descending length-two image between consecutive maxima; a direct length-two check excludes it. Independent aligned windows give the stated exponential bound. For the sextic, splitting every binary prefix after its last 1 gives I_2 I_2 all binary words, which yields the stated rational A_3 and the sextic as its denominator minus z times its numerator. Decimal bisection (`python /workspace/branches/frozen_replay.py 5`) gives lambda_4=3.5503790656826695146745…. The frozen enumeration was read as bounded corroboration, not a proof for arbitrary lengths.
